acakostic11: Nobody asked Teodor Acakostic why he came. Nobody in R-F13 asks that. He was handed a spade before he was handed a rifle.
Teodor Acakostic answered the first call, number 10 on the rolls. Somebody chalked the number on his helmet. It has not washed off yet.
Teodor Acakostic measured the remaining pencil against the remaining paper. For once, the supplies seemed likely to run out together.

At Calvary Farm, Teodor Acakostic of the Hegemony and Yann Vee of the Concord traded insults across the wire for an hour. By the end they were trading recipes. The Concord took Verdel Ridge. Teodor Acakostic watched the officer move a pin on the map and ask for more digging tools.
An unexploded shell lay beside the approach trench. Teodor Acakostic helped steer the carrying party around it and was glad to leave the problem to somebody else.
Teodor Acakostic fired at a movement across the wire at R-F13. The man went down: Florian "Mud" Spencerbonth, gravely wounded.

A shell burst in the trench at R-F13. Teodor Acakostic was thrown against the wall and did not get up. The bearers came at a run. The beds were full. Teodor Acakostic waits on a stretcher in the dark with a medic's promise and a dry mouth. Hill 304 fell to the Hegemony at dusk. Teodor Acakostic helped drag the guns up the slope and slept that night on ground nobody else had held for years.
Teodor Acakostic spent the day on a stretcher outside the aid post, waiting for a bed to come free. The bearers brought water twice.
Teodor Acakostic never saw the inside of the aid post. The medics changed his dressings on the stretcher until the wound closed. He is back on the line.
Teodor Acakostic raised his head for a heartbeat too long at R-F13. The bullet only grazed him. He will not do it again. Shot by Marek Ham of the Concord (@rals.ham).

A bullet went into Teodor Acakostic's chest just under the heart at R-F13. The medic said not to give him water, and then said nothing more. Shot by Florian "Mud" Spencerbonth of the Concord (@spencerbonthoux). The bearers reached Teodor Acakostic at R-F13 too late. One shot, and it was over. Shot by Florian "Mud" Spencerbonth of the Concord (@spencerbonthoux).

Walter "Crow" Acakostic arrived carrying the family name of Teodor Acakostic. The corporal asked how to pronounce his first name, and waited for the answer. Walter "Crow" Acakostic is one of the first hundred to answer the call. He wears the ribbon of the First Wave.
dick_j0b: The quartermaster asked Arno Dick to sign for the blanket. He examined the blanket and asked whether the holes were included.
Arno Dick tried to sketch a horse from memory. The dugout agreed it was a very good dog. Mail came up the line with a letter for Arno Dick. Arno Dick read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

A shell landed square in S-F19. They found Arno Dick alive under the sandbags, barely. Every minute counts now. An orderly waved the bearers in: one bed, cleared and scrubbed. Arno Dick was lifted onto it in the hospital dugout. Arno Dick opened his eyes today and asked for water. At S-F19 they cheered when the news came up the line. Hill 304 has been won. Arno Dick listened as the corporal read the news twice, once for the men just off watch.

Arno Dick slept most of the day. When he woke, someone had left a cup of tea on the crate beside the bed. Mail came up the line with a letter for Arno Dick. Arno Dick read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

Arno Dick never saw the inside of the aid post. The medics changed his dressings on the stretcher until the wound closed. He is back on the line. Mail came up the line with a letter for Arno Dick. Arno Dick read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.
Arno Dick drew a line on the bench to settle an argument about space. Everyone obeyed it until the broadest man returned from duty.

A parcel arrived tied with blue ribbon. Arno Dick gave the contents away and kept the ribbon to mark a page. Mail came up the line with a letter for Arno Dick. Arno Dick read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.
femboy_green: The new sniper gave his name as Wendel Green. The corporal looked at his boots, then at the mud, and laughed for the first time in a week.
The first hundred were recognised, and Wendel Green was among them. He wrote the news on the back of an unfinished letter.
Wendel Green held a letter up to the daylight to read the faint last lines. They were only a shopping list, written on reused paper.

Wendel Green noticed a loophole that had been dark for days. He watched it until dusk and wrote down the change. Verdel Ridge is in Concord hands. Wendel Green stopped arguing about the next watch and went to check the stores.
At the Sunken Road, Wendel Green of the Hegemony and Oskar Eddie of the Concord spent the morning shooting at the same loose sheet of metal. The sheet kept winning.
Dawn watch. Wendel Green put a round across no man's land and the enemy line went quiet: Gideon Actioncam, grazed.

Wendel Green noticed regular flashes from a gap beneath a roof beam. The position looks obvious enough to make him suspicious. The report confirmed the Hegemony victory at Hill 304. Wendel Green folded the paper so the headline stayed on the outside.
A loose thread in Wendel Green's blanket turned out to be very long. By the time he stopped pulling, there was a hole to explain.
A bullet clipped Wendel Green's helmet at R-F15 and took a strip of scalp with it. He bled into his collar, swore, and lay low. Shot by Jonas "Owl" Askey of the Concord (@roman_askey_).
Wendel Green came back to the squad today. The men had kept his spot on the fire step and his spoon.
Wendel Green watched a gap beneath a roof beam through another shift. The flash returns at the same angle, even when nothing else moves.
hi.its.guy: Severin Guy left a younger sister who sends drawings behind in Belmonte and came up the line with a key to a house that is no longer there. The men noticed at once that he laughs at exactly the wrong moments.
Severin Guy of the Concord and Severin Heheheha of the Hegemony watched a broken branch near Hill 304 all morning. Neither could risk assuming it was only a branch.

A bullet clipped Severin Guy's helmet at S-F20 and took a strip of scalp with it. He bled into his collar, swore, and lay low. Shot by Oskar "Whistle" Wiwiwib of the Hegemony (@wiwiwib3). News of the loss of Hill 304 reached S-F20 with the rations. Severin Guy ate while listening to the revised orders.
A bullet found Severin Guy at S-F20, high in the shoulder. He went down hard and stayed down. Shot by Walter Juizy of the Hegemony (@juizy_44).
A bed came free in the hospital dugout, and Severin Guy was carried in at last.
An orderly read the newspaper aloud in the ward. Severin Guy fell asleep halfway through the war news, which was the point.
For days Severin Guy was too weak to sit up on the stretcher. This morning he sat up, then stood, then asked for his rifle.
reza_zdsh: Nobody saw Silas Zdsh arrive. One morning there was simply one more helmet in S-F10, and a quiet field cook under it.
The colonel shook hands with the first hundred, one by one. Silas Zdsh was number 21. He still remembers how cold the colonel's glove was.
Silas Zdsh tried to write neatly for the first line of a letter. By the third, he was writing as quickly as the thoughts arrived.
Yann Vee (Concord) and Silas Zdsh (Hegemony) met in the same shell hole at Calvary Farm during a raid. They stared at each other. Then each crawled home, and neither has told anyone.
Edmund Matteozrybak wrote a letter for Silas Zdsh's mother, because Silas could not find the words. Silas signed it.
Edmund Acquillae taught Silas Zdsh to play the harmonica. The bay has asked them both, formally, to stop.

Marek Red (Concord) and Silas Zdsh (Hegemony) spotted the same abandoned cart near Calvary Farm. A long exchange of shots left the cart exactly where it was. From Verdel Ridge the Concord guns have a clear view. Silas Zdsh wrote to his mother, who writes every Sunday that night and said only: 'We will take it back.'
The salvo walked along S-F10 and caught Silas Zdsh in the open. Two men carried him back between salvos. A bed came free in the hospital dugout, and Silas Zdsh was carried in at last.
Another quiet day in the ward for Silas Zdsh. He counted the cracks in the ceiling and got to forty-one.

Silas Zdsh spent the night on a stretcher in the trench behind the aid post. Every bed was taken. Hill 304 fell to the Hegemony at dusk. Silas Zdsh helped drag the guns up the slope and slept that night on ground nobody else had held for years.
Silas Zdsh never saw the inside of the aid post. The medics changed his dressings on the stretcher until the wound closed. He is back on the line.
Silas Zdsh (Hegemony) and Otto "Saint" Kamdensipple (Concord) ended up in the same shell hole at the Drowned Farm. They stared at each other. Then each crawled home, and neither has told anyone.
Silas Zdsh counted the ladles in the pot against the men in the queue. The last serving took some careful scraping.
Someone returned an empty pot polished with bread. Silas Zdsh accepted it as a review.
simohayha2405: Henrik "Smokes" Simohayha came up with a draft of replacements on Day 8. Nobody asked his name until the third night. After that, everyone knew it.
Severin Martinsatali of the Concord lost a harmonica in no man's land at Verdel Ridge. Henrik "Smokes" Simohayha of the Hegemony found it and has been learning the enemy's songs on it.
